Formal votes are taken for major procedural and methodological decisions, for draft recommendations before posting, for final recommendations, and for statements about clinical practice. Votes may be taken for other decisions at the discretion of the Chair(s).

#### 7.4.1 General Voting Procedures

All motions on recommendations (at any stage) requiring a vote are passed when two thirds of the current Task Force membership vote "yes." Votes are taken by voice, hand, or email, without secret ballots.

For the first time, a federal advisory panel is set to recommend that women ages 30 to 65 be screened for cervical cancer primarily with an HPV test rather than the traditional Pap smear. ## Details of the proposed change

Under the USPSTF’s current guidance, women in the 30‑to‑65 age group could choose among three strategies: a Pap test every three years, an HPV test every five years, or a combination of both tests every five years. The new draft would eliminate the Pap‑only option for that age range, directing clinicians to use HPV testing at five‑year intervals. Women ages 21 to 29 would continue to receive Pap testing every three years, as before.

The panel’s recommendation carries practical weight because the Affordable Care Act requires most private insurers to cover services endorsed by the USPSTF without cost‑sharing. Consequently, a shift toward HPV testing could affect millions of women’s out‑of‑pocket expenses.
